classification.difficultyReason: Part c requires reframing the concave shape as two triangles sharing a base, recognising that their unknown heights differ by 8 cm, and cancelling the unknown contribution. Other parts require inferred dimensions and subtraction of rectangular or circular regions.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of the following shapes. Where needed, give an exact answer and an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Top horizontal segment and two vertical sides with an upward semicircular indentation tangent to the top at its midpoint. No bottom diameter is drawn.
spec.mathematics: Both vertical sides are 6 cm; the centre cue and tangency establish semicircle radius 6 cm and enclosing rectangle width 12 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and centre cue are visible.

answer.worked:
The semicircle has radius $6\text{ cm}$, so the enclosing rectangle is $12\text{ cm}$ wide.
$$\begin{align*}A&=12\times6-\frac12\pi\times6^2\\A&=72-18\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx15.45\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rectangle with a central bottom notch, matching ticks on three horizontal segments, six right-angle markers and highlighted overall-width and top-strip-height arrows.
spec.mathematics: Overall width 18 cm and height 12 cm; top strip height 5 cm; the three ticked horizontal segments are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Inferred notch dimensions and area are withheld.

answer.worked:
The three marked horizontal lengths are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Notch width}&=18\div3=6\text{ cm}\\\text{Notch height}&=12-5=7\text{ cm}\\A&=18\times12-6\times7\\A&=216-42\\A&=174\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right-pointing concave quadrilateral with equal outer edges, equal inner edges and external dimension arrows. Coordinates express the shape without supplying an additional length.
spec.mathematics: Left vertices have vertical separation 10 cm. The horizontal distance from the inward vertex to the right tip is 8 cm, not the entire horizontal extent.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two source measurements and equal-edge markings are visible.

answer.short:
$40\text{ cm}^2$.

Subtract the smaller triangle from the larger triangle, using their common $10\text{ cm}$ base.
answer.worked:
Both pairs of equal edges place the inward vertex and right tip on the perpendicular bisector of the $10\text{ cm}$ segment. Let the smaller triangle's perpendicular height be $h\text{ cm}$; the larger triangle's height is $(h+8)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times10(h+8)-\frac12\times10h\\A&=5h+40-5h\\A&=40\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Equal top and bottom horizontal edges with two inward-facing semicircular boundaries. No vertical diameter boundaries are added.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal width 10 cm; vertical separation and both semicircle diameters 8 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source dimensions, ticks and outline are visible.

answer.worked:
Each semicircle has radius $8\div2=4\text{ cm}$. Together they have the area of one circle.
$$\begin{align*}A&=10\times8-\pi\times4^2\\A&=80-16\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx29.73\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
